lastCompletedStory.title: Pin the /$bunfs/ compiled self-invoke premise with a real compiled-binary integration test

nextStoryContext: test/integration/self-invoke-compiled.test.ts empirically pins the /$bunfs/ premise resolveSelfInvokeArgv (src/util/self-invoke.ts) keys on, closing the gap left by every prior pure-unit / monkeypatch test of this bug class (test/commands/run-orch-resolver-compiled-mode.test.ts, test/retry/interactive.test.ts): it runs a REAL `bun build --compile` of a dynamically-written fixture (written into a fresh mkdtempSync tmpdir per test, never a permanently-committed fixture file) that imports resolveSelfInvokeArgv from src/ via an absolute import.meta.dir-derived path, then self-spawns itself with `[...resolveSelfInvokeArgv(execPath, argv1), markerToken]` in both compiled and interpreted mode and asserts the marker round-trips to the child's argv[2]. Three empirically-confirmed gotchas are documented in the new patterns.md bullet and must be respected by any FUTURE test that spawns a compiled binary from within `bun test`: (1) `bun build --compile`'s `.bun-build` scratch file lands in the build subprocess's OWN cwd (not near outfile/source) -- pin cwd to the same tmpdir being cleaned up in afterEach (CAM-407 leak-class discipline); (2) a compiled binary's own argv always reserves 2 slots ([0] literal "bun", [1] the /$bunfs/ virtual entry) before real args start at index 2, mirroring interpreted mode's [0]=bunPath,[1]=scriptPath shape closely enough that "is argv[2] defined" is a mode-agnostic child-vs-initial-run signal; process.execPath inside a compiled binary is its OWN path, never the literal "bun" (that's argv[0] only); (3) a nested spawnSync self-spawn chain (bun test -> compiled binary -> its own self-spawned child) hangs past bun test's 5000ms default timeout unless `stdin: 'ignore'` is set at EVERY level of the chain -- the identical chain run from a plain `bun script.ts` outside bun:test needed no such option and completed in <200ms, so this is bun:test-process-specific, not a general bun quirk. No new file-size-budget entry was needed (the new test file is unlisted in scripts/file-size-budget.json, which only enforces listed files). scripts/cam/project.toml showed a stray uncommitted diff (a `resend_from` key appearing after running the check:all spine against the live repo, source not investigated) that was reverted via `git checkout --` before committing since it was unrelated to this story's scope -- flagging in case a future story's gate run reproduces the same stray diff, so it isn't mistaken for that story's own change.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Docs confirm /$bunfs/ is Bun's real, intentional internal path prefix for embedded-file virtual paths produced by `import ... with { type: 'file' }` ("Replaces the import with an internal path (prefixed with /$bunfs/)"). The docs do not separately document process.argv[1]'s exact compiled-mode value (that remains an empirically-observed behavior, as already recorded in prior patterns.md entries for CAM-425/426), but the prefix itself is a documented, stable Bun convention, not an implementation accident this test is pinning against undocumented behavior alone.
